title: Freyja and the making of a European defense industry
gist: PIIE/Bruegel/KSE authors argue Freyja, a Europe-Ukraine anti-ballistic interceptor at ~$700k (one-fifth of a Patriot, prototype mid-2027), should anchor a scaled Europe-Ukraine defense JV system. With 180+ B2B partnerships but >20% stalling, small EU programs and a 2027 Ukrainian funding gap, they call for multiyear purchase commitments to make JVs bankable.

themes.theme: Freyja: European anti-ballistic alternative to Patriot

insights.claim: Freyja, a joint Europe-Ukraine anti-ballistic missile-defense project referenced in von der Leyen's September 2026 State of the Union, is estimated at about $700,000 per interceptor, roughly one-fifth the cost of a US Patriot missile, with a prototype possible by mid-2027.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: A sub-$1M European interceptor would reshape air-defense procurement economics and challenge US incumbents' pricing power in Europe.
insights.quote: At an estimated $700,000 per interceptor, Freyja—for which there could be a prototype by mid-2027—could offer a European-produced alternative at roughly one-fifth of the cost of a Patriot missile.
insights.locator: Patriot interceptors from the United States

insights.claim: US Patriot interceptors are becoming harder to obtain, and buying more Patriots with EU money will not fix the structural supply shortfall, making a pan-European missile-defense system critical.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Structural interceptor scarcity supports sustained demand for European air-defense producers rather than a one-off procurement spike.
insights.quote: Buying some additional Patriots with EU money will not solve the structural supply problem.
insights.locator: Patriot interceptors from the United States

insights.claim: Freyja pools companies and technology from Ukraine, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom, making it a broad multinational industrial consortium rather than a single-national program.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Contract flows may be spread across many national defense suppliers, diluting single-company upside but broadening the beneficiary set.
insights.locator: Patriot interceptors from the United States

insights.claim: A Europe-produced missile-defense system developed with Ukraine would reduce European dependence on the US and help restore deterrence in Europe.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Strategic autonomy push implies durable policy support for European-sourced air defense over US imports.
insights.quote: A European missile-defense system developed with Ukraine and produced in Europe will reduce dependence on the US and restore deterrence in Europe.

themes.theme: Ukraine as battlefield test lab and innovation engine

insights.claim: Combat testing in Ukraine can make European defense firms world-class by letting them integrate decades of component work (sensors, radars, guidance electronics) into complete active defense systems refined against a sophisticated enemy.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: European primes with Ukrainian combat-validated products gain a competitive export edge.
insights.quote: Second, testing weapons in real combat in Ukraine will give European defense firms an opportunity to become world-class.
insights.locator: Second, testing weapons in real combat

insights.claim: In Ukraine the battlefield-to-factory feedback loop has compressed from decades to weeks and months, supported by the established Brave1 Test in Ukraine program.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Iteration speed, not just scale, becomes the key competitive variable for defense suppliers.
insights.quote: In Ukraine, the feedback loop between the battlefield and the factory has been compressed into weeks and months, rather than decades
insights.locator: Second, testing weapons in real combat

insights.claim: Modular, rapidly upgradable defense systems built under wartime cost and time pressure will spill over into civilian advances in manufacturing, software-hardware interaction, sensor fusion and supply-chain resilience, analogous to Cold War defense research seeding satellite navigation and the internet.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Dual-use spillovers widen the investable theme beyond defense primes to industrial tech, sensors and software.
insights.quote: innovation that comes out of Europe-Ukraine cooperation will not stay within the defense sector.

insights.claim: At least 180 international business-to-business defense partnerships involving Ukraine have been formed, 20% with German firms, 10% with Danish firms and 9% with US firms.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Germany and Denmark are the leading industrial partners and likely first beneficiaries of scaled joint ventures.
insights.quote: At least 180 international business-to-business partnerships involving Ukraine

insights.claim: More than one in five Europe-Ukraine defense industrial partnerships stalled after launch.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Announcement-to-execution risk is material; headline partnership counts overstate realized capacity.
insights.quote: More than one in five Europe-Ukraine industrial partnerships stalled postlaunch.

insights.claim: Europe-Ukraine defense partnerships led by private Ukrainian firms succeed about 96% of the time versus 62% for those led by state-owned enterprises, a gap the authors attribute to cooperation depending on informal speed and flexibility rather than predictable rules.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Favor partnerships anchored by private Ukrainian firms; SOE-led ventures carry markedly higher failure risk.
insights.quote: The gap reflects how much cooperation depends on informal speed and flexibility, rather than predictable rules.

insights.claim: Denmark's model of channeling funds directly through Ukraine's Defence Procurement Agency with strong oversight has proved scalable, while faster bilateral deals by other partners lack shared mechanisms for prioritization and monitoring.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: The 'Danish model' is the template most likely to be codified and scaled multilaterally.

insights.claim: Delays in tying pledged foreign security money to Ukrainian reforms mean Ukraine's 2027 draft budget risks underfunding defense for lack of external support.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: A 2027 Ukrainian defense funding gap raises pressure for new EU/multilateral financing vehicles.

insights.claim: From 2027, a significant share of Ukraine's defense production will need to come from joint ventures with European firms, both to replace some US systems and to meet new Russian threats.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Signals a structural shift of Ukraine's supply base from US systems toward European JV output.
insights.quote: From 2027, a significant share of Ukraine's defense production will have to come from joint ventures with European firms

insights.claim: Existing EU programs (EDIP, SAFE and the Ukraine Investment Framework) are small and presuppose Ukrainian firms already hold large contracts, which a cash-constrained Ukrainian procurement budget cannot guarantee.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Current EU defense instruments are mis-designed for Ukraine JVs; expect calls for larger, differently structured funding.
insights.quote: A cash-constrained Ukrainian procurement budget cannot guarantee such contracts.

themes.theme: Scaling via multiyear commitments and multilateral vehicles

insights.claim: Options to scale Europe-Ukraine defense cooperation include codifying Danish-style funding through multilateral vehicles such as the Defence, Security, and Resilience Bank or a Multilateral Defence Mechanism, or a new EU-Ukraine cooperation agreement.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Watch which vehicle is chosen; it will determine the scale and conditionality of JV financing.

insights.claim: EU support should shift from project-by-project grants to multiyear purchase commitments large enough to make Europe-Ukraine defense joint ventures bankable.
insights.speaker: Elina Ribakova,Nataliia Shapoval,Guntram B. Wolff
insights.so_what: Multiyear offtake commitments would unlock private/bank financing and capacity investment in defense JVs.
insights.quote: There should be a move from project-by-project grants to multiyear purchase commitments large enough to make joint ventures bankable in Europe.
